SMTO-EXE-0249 — This Docker option isn't supported by SMTO

GUID: acfd03f5-7227-588b-af68-1a3a77eba7e0
Slug: docker-unsupported-option
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Your request used something SMTO's Docker support can't do safely, such as shortcut links in the build folder or showing only one kind of Compose log output. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were building an image, remove any shortcut links (symlinks) in the build folder and put real copies of those files there instead. SMTO only packs ordinary files that are really inside the build folder, so links to other places are refused.
  2. If you don't need those linked files in the image, list them in the folder's .dockerignore file instead. Files listed in .dockerignore are left out of the build, so they no longer cause the refusal.
  3. If you asked for Compose logs, ask for the normal and error output together rather than only one of them. Docker Compose can't separate the two kinds of output, so SMTO always shows them together.

What success looks like

  • The build or log request runs and SMTO shows the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't move the build folder's links to point somewhere else; any link is refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Docker adapter rejected an unsupported option: the build context contains symlinks, paths resolving outside the context, or special files, or Compose logs requested stdout and stderr separately, which Compose cannot do.

What this means

  • Build-context validation found links/paths outside its supported archive contract, or Compose logs requested independently selected stdout/stderr streams that this adapter cannot separate. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Build-context validation found links/paths outside its supported archive contract, or Compose logs requested independently selected stdout/stderr streams that this adapter cannot separate.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the unsupported context feature or log-channel combination and inspect whether a supported form meets the task.

How to fix it

  • Replace symlinks and special files in context_path with regular files, or exclude them through .dockerignore, so every included entry is a regular file inside the context. For Compose logs, request both stdout and stderr (the default).
  • Use a supported build context or Compose log-channel selection; keep rejected path and scope protections intact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported explicit option preserves intended scope without weakening file or transport boundaries.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
